sa: यो ह वै ज्येष्ठं च श्रेष्ठं च वेद ज्येष्ठश् च ह वै श्रेष्ठश् च भवति ।
प्राणो वाव ज्येष्ठश् च श्रेष्ठश् च ॥
iast: yo ha vai jyeṣṭhaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ ca veda jyeṣṭhaś ca ha vai śreṣṭhaś ca bhavati ।
prāṇo vāva jyeṣṭhaś ca śreṣṭhaś ca ॥

tr.text: Om, Verily, he who knows the eldest and the best, surely becomes the eldest and the best. Prana is indeed the eldest and the best (of the organs).

sa: यो ह वै वसिष्ठं वेद वसिष्ठो ह स्वानां भवति ।
iast: yo ha vai vasiṣṭhaṃ veda vasiṣṭho ha svānāṃ bhavati ।

tr.text: Verily, he who knows the richest, becomes the richest among his own people. Speech is indeed the richest.

sa: यो ह वै प्रतिष्ठां वेद प्रति ह तिष्ठत्य् अस्मिंश् च लोके ऽमुष्मिंश् च ।
iast: yo ha vai pratiṣṭhāṃ veda prati ha tiṣṭhaty asmiṃś ca loke ’muṣmiṃś ca ।

tr.text: Verily, he who knows the stable basis, becomes stabilized in this world and in the next. The eye is indeed the stable basis.

sa: यो ह वै संपदं वेद सं हास्मै कामाः पद्यन्ते दैवाश् च मानुषाश् च ।
iast: yo ha vai saṃpadaṃ veda saṃ hāsmai kāmāḥ padyante daivāś ca mānuṣāś ca ।

tr.text: Verily, he who knows prosperity, attains all desires, both divine and human. The ear is indeed prosperity.

sa: यो ह वा आयतनं वेदायतनं ह स्वानां भवति ।
iast: yo ha vā āyatanaṃ vedāyatanaṃ ha svānāṃ bhavati ।

tr.text: Verily, he who knows the abode, becomes the abode of his people. The mind is indeed the abode.

sa: अहं श्रेयान् अस्म्य् अहं श्रेयान् अस्मीति ॥
iast: ahaṃ śreyān asmy ahaṃ śreyān asmīti ॥

tr.text: Now, once the five senses disputed among themselves about their personal superiority, saying ‘I am superior’.

sa: ते ह प्राणाः प्रजापतिं पितरम् एत्योचुः भगवन् को नः श्रेष्ठ इति ।
यस्मिन् व उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं पापिष्ठतरम् इव दृश्येत स वः श्रेष्ठ इति ॥
iast: te ha prāṇāḥ prajāpatiṃ pitaram etyocuḥ bhagavan ko naḥ śreṣṭha iti ।
yasmin va utkrānte śarīraṃ pāpiṣṭhataram iva dṛśyeta sa vaḥ śreṣṭha iti ॥

tr.text: Those senses approached the father Prajapati and said to him, ‘Revered sir, who is the best amongst us ?’ He replied, ‘He amongst you is the best on whose departure the body would appear its worst, as it were.’

sa: यथा कला अवदन्तः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन पश्यन्तश् चक्षुषा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेण ध्यायन्तो मनसैवम् इति ।
iast: yathā kalā avadantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivam iti ।
words: mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)

tr.text: Speech departed. Staying a year out, it came back and asked, ‘How have you been able to live without me ?’ (The others replied,) ‘Just like the dumb, though not speaking, yet living with the breath, seeing with the eyes, hearing with the ear and thinking with the mind.’ (At this) speech entered (the body).

sa: यथान्धा अपश्यन्तः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन वदन्तो वाचा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेण ध्यायन्तो मनसैवम् इति ।
iast: yathāndhā apaśyantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivam iti ।
words: mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)

tr.text: The eye departed. Staying a year out, it came back and asked, ‘How have you been able to live without me ?’ (The others replied,) ‘Just like the blind, though not seeing, yet living with the breath, speaking with the organ of speech, hearing with the ear and thinking with the mind.’ (At this) the eye entered (the body).

sa: तत् संवत्सरं प्रोष्य पर्येत्योवाच कथम् अशकतर्ते मज् जीवितुम् इति ।
यथा बधिरा अशृण्वन्तः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन वदन्तो वाचा पश्यन्तश् चक्षुषा ध्यायन्तो मनसैवम् इति ।
iast: tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣya paryetyovāca katham aśakatarte maj jīvitum iti ।
yathā badhirā aśṛṇvantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā dhyāyanto manasaivam iti ।
words: not hearing or liking to hear
mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)

tr.text: The ear departed. Staying a year out, it came back and asked, ‘How have you been able to live without me ?’ (The others replied,) ‘Just like the deaf, though not hearing, yet living with the breath, speaking with the organ of speech, seeing with the eye and thinking with the mind.’ (At this) the ear entered (the body).

sa: यथा बाला अमनसः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन वदन्तो वाचा पश्यन्तश् चक्षुषा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेणैवम् इति ।
iast: yathā bālā amanasaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇaivam iti ।

tr.text: The mind departed. Staying a year out, it came back and asked, ‘How have you been able to live without me ?’ (The others replied,) ‘Just like infants without developed minds, yet living with the breath, speaking with the organ of speech, seeing with the eye and hearing with the ear.’ (At this) the mind entered (the body).

sa: अथ ह प्राण उच्चिक्रमिषन् स यथा सुहयः पड्वीशशङ्कून् संखिदेद् एवम् इतरान् प्राणान् समखिदत् ।
iast: atha ha prāṇa uccikramiṣan sa yathā suhayaḥ paḍvīśaśaṅkūn saṃkhided evam itarān prāṇān samakhidat ।

tr.text: Then, as the Prana was about to depart, it uprooted the other senses just as a horse of mettle would uproot the pegs to which it is tethered. They all then came to it and said, ‘O revered sir, be our lord, you are the best amongst us; do not depart from the body.’

sa: यद् अहं वसिष्ठो ऽस्मि त्वं तद्वसिष्ठो ऽसीति ।

tr.text: Then speech said to that one, ‘Just as I am the richest, in the same manner are you also the richest’. Then the eye said to that one, ‘Just as I am the stable basis, in the same manner are you also the stable basis’.

sa: यद् अहं संपद् अस्मि त्वं तत्संपद् असीति ।
यद् अहम् आयतनम् अस्मि त्वं तदायतनम् असीति ॥
iast: yad ahaṃ saṃpad asmi tvaṃ tatsaṃpad asīti ।
yad aham āyatanam asmi tvaṃ tadāyatanam asīti ॥

tr.text: Then the ear said to that one, ‘Just as I am prosperity, in the same manner are you also prosperity.’ Then the mind said to that one, ‘Just as I am the abode, in the same manner are you also the abode.’

sa: न वै वाचो न चक्षूंषि न श्रोत्राणि न मनांसीत्य् आचक्षते ।
iast: na vai vāco na cakṣūṃṣi na śrotrāṇi na manāṃsīty ācakṣate ।
words: mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)

tr.text: Verily, people do not call them as organs of speech, nor as eyes, nor as ears, nor as minds. But they call them only as Pranas; for the Prana indeed is all these.

sa: स होवाच किं मे ऽन्नं भविष्यतीति ।
यत् किंचिद् इदम् आ श्वभ्य आ शकुनिभ्य इति होचुः ।
न ह वा एवंविदि किंचनानन्नं भवतीति ॥
iast: yat kiṃcid idam ā śvabhya ā śakunibhya iti hocuḥ ।
na ha vā evaṃvidi kiṃcanānannaṃ bhavatīti ॥
words: a bird (esp. a large bird = gridhra or cilla)

tr.text: He (the Prana) asked, ‘What will be my food?’ ‘Whatever there is here, even (the food) of dogs and birds’, replied the senses. Whatever is eaten, all that is the food of Ana. The name "Ana’ indeed is self-evident. For him who knows thus there is nothing that is not food.

sa: स होवाच किं मे वासो भविष्यतीति ।
तस्माद् वा एतद् अशिष्यन्तः पुरस्ताच् चोपरिष्टाच् चाद्भिः परिदधति ।
iast: sa hovāca kiṃ me vāso bhaviṣyatīti ।
tasmād vā etad aśiṣyantaḥ purastāc copariṣṭāc cādbhiḥ paridadhati ।
words: to lay or put or place or set round

tr.text: He asked, ‘What will be my garments ?’ ‘Water’, replied the senses. Therefore, indeed, those who are about to eat, cover it, both before and after, with water. (He who knows thus) becomes the obtainer of clothes and of upper garments.

sa: तद् धैतत् सत्यकामो जाबालो गोश्रुतये वैयाघ्रपद्यायोक्त्वोवाच ।
यद्य् अप्य् एनच् छुष्काय स्थाणवे ब्रूयाज् जायेरन्न् एवास्मिञ् छाखाः प्ररोहेयुः पलाशानीति ॥
iast: tad dhaitat satyakāmo jābālo gośrutaye vaiyāghrapadyāyoktvovāca ।
yady apy enac chuṣkāya sthāṇave brūyāj jāyerann evāsmiñ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ॥
words: name of a man with the patr. Vaiyāghrapadya

tr.text: Satyakama Jabala imparted this (doctrine of Prana) to Gosruti, the son of Vyaghrapada, and said, ‘If anyone should impart this even to a dry stump, then branches would certainly shoot and leaves would sprout from it’.

sa: अथ यदि महज् जिगमिषेत्, अमावास्यायाम् दीक्षित्वा पौर्णमास्यां रात्रौ सर्वौषधस्य मन्थम् दधिमधुनोर् उपमथ्य ज्येष्ठाय श्रेष्ठाय स्वाहेत्य् अग्नाव् आज्यस्य हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् अवनयेत् ॥
iast: atha yadi mahaj jigamiṣet, amāvāsyāyām dīkṣitvā paurṇamāsyāṃ rātrau sarvauṣadhasya mantham dadhimadhunor upamathya jyeṣṭhāya śreṣṭhāya svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet ॥

tr.text: Next, if that knower of Prana desires to attain greatness, then having consecrated himself on the new moon day, he should, on the full moon night, stir up in a vessel of curd and honey the mash of all herbs and then offer an oblation into the fire on the spot prescribed for offerings, with the Mantra, ‘Svaha to the eldest and the best’, and throw what remains attached to the ladle into the mash-pot.

iast: sa mā jyaiṣṭhyaṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ rājyam ādhipatyaṃ gamayatu ।

tr.text: Then, moving a little away and taking the mash-pot in his hands, he should recite (the Mantra): ‘You are Ama by name, for all this (universe) rests with you. He (i.e. you as Prana) is the eldest, the best, the effulgent, and sovereign. May he (i.e. you as Prana) lead me to the eldest age, to the best position, to effulgence, and to sovereignty. Verily I wish to become all this.’

sa: निर्णिज्य कंसं चमसं वा पश्चाद् अग्नेः संविशति ।
चर्मणि वा स्थण्डिले वा वाचंयमो ऽप्रसाहः ।
स यदि स्त्रियं पश्येत् समृद्धं कर्मेति विद्यात् ॥
iast: nirṇijya kaṃsaṃ camasaṃ vā paścād agneḥ saṃviśati ।

tr.text: Then, reciting this Rik-mantra, foot by foot, he should sip. ‘We pray for that food pertaining to the Progenitor’, saying this (line) he should sip. ‘We pray for the food of the effulgent one’, saying this he should sip. ‘(Which is) the best and all-sustaining’, saying this he should sip. We readily meditate upon (the form of the deity) Bhaga’, saying this and washing the pot shaped like a Kamsa (goblet) or a Camasa (cup), he should drink all. Then he should lie down behind the fire on a skin or on the ground, controlling speech and mind. If he should see a woman (in a dream), he should know that his rite has succeeded.

sa: यदा कर्मसु काम्येषु स्त्रियं स्वप्नेषु पश्यति ।
समृद्धिं तत्र जानीयात् तस्मिन् स्वप्ननिदर्शने तस्मिन् स्वप्ननिदर्शने ॥

tr.text: There is this verse about it: During the performance of the rites for desired results if the performer sees a woman in a dream, then he should recognize fulfilment in this vision in a dream – yea, in this vision in a dream.

name of a warrior-tribe and their country in the north of India; name of a Vedic school

tr.text: Once Svetaketu, the grandson of Aruna, came to the assembly of the Panchalas. Pravahana, the son of Jivala, enquired of him, ‘My boy, has your father instructed you ?’ ‘He has indeed, revered sir’.

sa: वेत्थ यद् इतो ऽधि प्रजाः प्रयन्तीति ।
वेत्थ पथोर् देवयानस्य पितृयाणस्य च व्यावर्तना ३ इति ।
iast: vettha pathor devayānasya pitṛyāṇasya ca vyāvartanā 3 iti ।
words: turn (of a road); coil (of a snake); turning away

tr.text: ‘Do you know where created beings go above from here ?’ No, revered sir’. ‘Do you know the place of parting of the two paths – the path of the gods and the path of the fathers ?’ ‘No, revered sir’.

sa: वेत्थ यथासौ लोको न संपूर्यत ३ इति ।
वेत्थ यथा पञ्चम्याम् आहुताव् आपः पुरुषवचसो भवन्तीति ।
iast: vettha yathāsau loko na saṃpūryata 3 iti ।
vettha yathā pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavantīti ।

tr.text: ‘Do you know why the other world is not filled up ?’ ‘No, revered sir’. ‘Do you know how, at the fifth oblation, the liquid oblations (or unseen results of action) come to be designated as man ?’ ‘No, indeed, revered sir’.

sa: अथानु किम् अनु शिष्ठो ऽवोचथा यो हीमानि न विद्यात् ।
तं होवाचाननुशिष्य वाव किल मा भगवान् अब्रवीद् अनु त्वाशिषम् इति ॥
iast: athānu kim anu śiṣṭho ’vocathā yo hīmāni na vidyāt ।
taṃ hovācānanuśiṣya vāva kila mā bhagavān abravīd anu tvāśiṣam iti ॥
words: to work hard; to exert one's self; to weary one's self

tr.text: ’Then why did you say, "I have been instructed" ? Foz, how can he who does not know these things say, "I have been instructed" ?’ He was distressed and came to his father’s place and said to him, ‘Revered Sir, wiuhout having instructed me properly you said, "I have instructed you".’

sa: स होवाच यथा मा त्वं तदैतान् अवदो यथाहम् एषां नैकंचन वेद ।
यद्य् अहम् इमान् अवेदिष्यं कथं ते नावक्ष्यम् इति ॥
iast: sa hovāca yathā mā tvaṃ tadaitān avado yathāham eṣāṃ naikaṃcana veda ।
yady aham imān avediṣyaṃ kathaṃ te nāvakṣyam iti ॥

tr.text: ‘That nominal Kshatriya asked me five questions, and I was not able to answer even one of them’. The father said, ‘Even as you have spoken to me about them, so do I not know even one of them. If I had known them, why should I not have toll you ?’

sa: स ह गौतमो राज्ञो ऽर्धम् एयाय ।
मानुषस्य भगवन् गौतम वित्तस्य वरं वृणीथा इति ।
याम् एव कुमारस्यान्ते वाचम् अभाषथास् ताम् एव मे ब्रूहीति ।
iast: mānuṣasya bhagavan gautama vittasya varaṃ vṛṇīthā iti ।
yām eva kumārasyānte vācam abhāṣathās tām eva me brūhīti ।

tr.text: Then Gautama went to the king’s place. When he arrived, the king made reverential offerings to him. In the morning he presented himself to the king when he was in the assembly. The king said to him, ‘O revered Gautama, please ask for a boon of human wealth’. He replied, ‘O king, let the human wealth remain with you, tell me those words which you spoke to my boy’. The king was perturbed.

sa: तं ह चिरं वसेत्य् आज्ञापयां चकार ।
यथेयं न प्राक् त्वत्तः पुरा विद्या ब्राह्मणान् गच्छति ।
तस्माद् उ सर्वेषु लोकेषु क्षत्रस्यैव प्रशासनम् अभूद् इति ।
iast: taṃ ha ciraṃ vasety ājñāpayāṃ cakāra ।
yatheyaṃ na prāk tvattaḥ purā vidyā brāhmaṇān gacchati ।
tasmād u sarveṣu lokeṣu kṣatrasyaiva praśāsanam abhūd iti ।
words: to order; to command; to direct

tr.text: The king commanded him, ‘Stay here for a long time.’ At the end of the period he said to him, ‘Even as you told me, O Gautama, prior to you, this knowledge never went to the Brahmanas. This is why the expounding of this knowledge belonged to the Kshatriyas in earlier times in all the worlds’. Then he instructed him.
The world yonder is indeed the fire, O Gautama. Of that, the sun is the fuel, the rays are the smoke, the day is the flame, the moon is the embers, and the stars are the sparks.

sa: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवाः श्रद्धां जुह्वति ।
iast: tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ śraddhāṃ juhvati ।

tr.text: Into this fire the deities offer the oblation of faith. Out of that oblation King Soma arises.

words: the thunderbolt; a flash of lightning; the tip of a missile

tr.text: Parjanya is indeed the fire, O Gautama. Of that, the air is the fuel, the cloud is the smoke, the lightning is the flame, the thunderbolt is the embers, and the rumblings of thunder are the sparks.

sa: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवाः सोमं राजानं जुह्वति ।
iast: tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ somaṃ rājānaṃ juhvati ।

tr.text: Into this fire the deities offer the oblation of King Soma. Out of that oblation rain arises.
The earth indeed is the fire, O Gautama. Of that, the year, is the fuel, Akasa is the smgke, night is the flame, the directions are the embers, and the intermediate directions are the sparks.

sa: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवा वर्षं जुह्वति ।
iast: tasminn etasminn agnau devā varṣaṃ juhvati ।

tr.text: Into this fire the deities offer the oblation of rain. Out of that oblation food (in the shape of corn) arises.
Man indeed is the fire, O Gautama. Of that, speech is the fuel, Prana is the smoke, the tongue is the flame, the eye is the embers, and the ear is the sparks.

sa: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवा अन्नं जुह्वति ।
iast: tasminn etasminn agnau devā annaṃ juhvati ।

tr.text: Into this fire the deities offer the oblation of food. Out of that oblation the seed arises.
Woman indeed is the fire, O Gautama. Into this fire the deities offer the oblation of the seed. Out of that oblation the foetus arises.

sa: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवा रेतो जुह्वति ।
iast: tasminn etasminn agnau devā reto juhvati ।

tr.text: Woman indeed is the fire, O Gautama. Into this fire the deities offer the oblation of the seed. Out of that oblation the foetus arises.

sa: इति तु पञ्चम्याम् आहुताव् आपः पुरुषवचसो भवन्तीति ।
स उल्बावृतो गर्भो दश वा नव वा मासान् अन्तः शयित्वा यावद् वाथ जायते ॥
iast: iti tu pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavantīti ।
sa ulbāvṛto garbho daśa vā nava vā māsān antaḥ śayitvā yāvad vātha jāyate ॥
words: a cover; envelope; the membrane surrounding the embryo

tr.text: Thus at the fifth oblation, (the oblation called) water comes to be designated as man. That foetus, covered with membrane, lies for nine or ten months, and is then born.

sa: तं प्रेतं दिष्टम् इतो ऽग्नय एव हरन्ति यत एवेतो यतः संभूतो भवति ॥
iast: taṃ pretaṃ diṣṭam ito ’gnaya eva haranti yata eveto yataḥ saṃbhūto bhavati ॥
words: as long as life lasts; for the whole of life

tr.text: Being born, he lives whatever the length of his life may be. When he is dead (to attain the world) as ordained, they carry him from here (for cremation) to fire itself from which alone he came and from which he arose.

sa: ये चेमे ऽरण्ये श्रद्धा तप इत्य् उपासते ।
आपूर्यमाणपक्षाद् यान् षड् उदङ्ङ् एति मासांस् तान् ॥
iast: ye ceme ’raṇye śraddhā tapa ity upāsate ।
āpūryamāṇapakṣād yān ṣaḍ udaṅṅ eti māsāṃs tān ॥

tr.text: Among them, those who know thus (this knowledge of the five fires) and those who are devoted to faith and austerity in the forest – they go to light; from light to the day, from the day to the bright fortnight, from the bright fortnight to those six months during which the sun travels northward; from the months to the year, from the year to the sun, from the sun to the moon and from the moon to the lightning. (From the region of Brahman) a person, who is other than human, (comes and) causes them, existing there, to attain Brahman. This is the path of the gods.

Among them, those who know thus (this knowledge of the five fires) and those who are devoted to faith and austerity in the forest – they go to light; from light to the day, from the day to the bright fortnight, from the bright fortnight to those six months during which the sun travels northward; from the months to the year, from the year to the sun, from the sun to the moon and from the moon to the lightning. (From the region of Brahman) a person, who is other than human, (comes and) causes them, existing there, to attain Brahman. This is the path of the gods.

sa: अथ य इमे ग्राम इष्टापूर्ते दत्तम् इत्य् उपासते ।
अपरपक्षाद् यान् षड् दक्षिणैति मासांस् तान् ।
iast: atha ya ime grāma iṣṭāpūrte dattam ity upāsate ।
aparapakṣād yān ṣaḍ dakṣiṇaiti māsāṃs tān ।
words: the latter half of the month; the other or opposing side; the defendant
the latter half of the month; the other or opposing side; the defendant

tr.text: But those who living in villages (as householders) practise sacrifices and works of public utility and gift, go to smoke, from smoke to night, from night to the dark fortnight, from the dark fortnight to those months during which the sun travels southward. From there they do not reach the year (like those going the path of the gods).

From the months, (they go) to the region of the fathers, from the region of the fathers to Akasa, from Akasa to the moon. This (i.e. this moon) is King Soma (the king of the Brahmanas). This is the food of the deities. This the deities eat.

sa: तस्मिन् यवात्संपातम् उषित्वाथैतम् एवाध्वानं पुनर् निवर्तन्ते ।
iast: tasmin yavātsaṃpātam uṣitvāthaitam evādhvānaṃ punar nivartante ।

tr.text: Residing in that (region of the moon) till they have exhausted (the results of action) they then return again the same way as they came (by the path that is being mentioned). They come to Akasa, and from Akasa to air. Having become air, they become smoke. Having become smoke they become the white cloud.

sa: त इह व्रीहियवा ओषधिवनस्पतयस् तिलमासा इति जायन्ते ऽतो वै खलु दुर्निष्प्रपतरम् ।
यो यो ह्य् अन्नम् अत्ति यो रेतः सिञ्चति तद् भूय एव भवति ॥
iast: ta iha vrīhiyavā oṣadhivanaspatayas tilamāsā iti jāyante ’to vai khalu durniṣprapataram ।
yo yo hy annam atti yo retaḥ siñcati tad bhūya eva bhavati ॥
words: to begin to rain; to rain; to shed or shower abundantly with

tr.text: Having become the white cloud, they become the (rain-bearing) cloud. Having become the cloud they fall as rain. Then they are born in this world as rice and barley, herbs and trees, sesamum plants and beans. But the release from these is more difficult, for whoever eats the food and sows the seed, they become like him only.

sa: तद् य इह रमणीयचरणा अभ्याशो ह यत् ते रमणीयां योनिम् आपद्येरन् ब्राह्मणयोनिं वा क्षत्रिययोनिं वा वैश्ययोनिं वा ।
अथ य इह कपूयचरणा अभ्याशो ह यत् ते कपूयां योनिम् आपद्येरञ् श्वयोनिम् वा सूकरयोनिं वा चण्डालयोनिं वा ॥
iast: tad ya iha ramaṇīyacaraṇā abhyāśo ha yat te ramaṇīyāṃ yonim āpadyeran brāhmaṇayoniṃ vā kṣatriyayoniṃ vā vaiśyayoniṃ vā ।
atha ya iha kapūyacaraṇā abhyāśo ha yat te kapūyāṃ yonim āpadyerañ śvayonim vā sūkarayoniṃ vā caṇḍālayoniṃ vā ॥
words: going round or about; motion; course
a member of the military or reigning order; a red horse; name of a people
going round or about; motion; course

tr.text: Among them, those who have good residual results of action here (earned in this world and left as residue after the enjoyment in the region of the moon), quickly reach a good womb, the womb of a Brahmana, or of a Kshatriya or of a Vaisya. But those who have bad residual results of action quickly reach an evil womb, the womb of a dog or of a hog or of a Chandala.

sa: अथैतयोः पथोर् न कतरेणचन तानीमानि क्षुद्राण्य् असकृदावर्तीनि भूतानि भवन्ति जायस्व म्रियस्वेति ।
iast: athaitayoḥ pathor na katareṇacana tānīmāni kṣudrāṇy asakṛdāvartīni bhūtāni bhavanti jāyasva mriyasveti ।
words: whirling or turning upon itself; returning
to detest; to abhor from; to seek to watch over

tr.text: Then, by neither of these two paths, do they go. They, as small creatures, keep repeatedly revolving, subject to the saying ‘Be born and die’. This is the third state. Therefore that region (of the moon) is never filled up. Hence one should be disgusted (with this state). There is this verse about it.

sa: एते पतन्ति चत्वारः पञ्चमश् चाचरंस् तैर् इति ॥
iast: ete patanti catvāraḥ pañcamaś cācaraṃs tair iti ॥
words: spirituous liquor; wine (in ancient times "a kind of beer")
to abide; to dwell; to spend (time)

tr.text: One who steals gold, one who drinks wine, one who dishonours the teacher’s bed, and one who injures a Brahmana – all these four fall, as also the fifth one who associates with them.

sa: अथ ह य एतान् एवं पञ्चाग्नीन् वेद न सह तैर् अप्य् आचरन् पाप्मना लिप्यते ।
शुद्धः पूतः पुण्यलोको भवति य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ॥
iast: atha ha ya etān evaṃ pañcāgnīn veda na saha tair apy ācaran pāpmanā lipyate ।
śuddhaḥ pūtaḥ puṇyaloko bhavati ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: Moreover, he who knows (worships) these five fires thus, even though he associates with those sinners, is not tainted by sin. He who knows these thus becomes cleansed and pure and obtains the meritorious world – yea, he who knows thus.

sa: प्राचीनशाल औपमन्यवः सत्ययज्ञः पौलुषिर् इन्द्रद्युम्नो भाल्लवेयो जनः शार्कराक्ष्यो बुडिल आश्वतराश्विस् ते हैते महाशाला महाश्रोत्रियाः समेत्य मीमांसां चक्रुः ।
iast: prācīnaśāla aupamanyavaḥ satyayajñaḥ pauluṣir indradyumno bhāllaveyo janaḥ śārkarākṣyo buḍila āśvatarāśvis te haite mahāśālā mahāśrotriyāḥ sametya mīmāṃsāṃ cakruḥ ।
words: a Brāhman versed in the Veda
profound thought or reflection or Consideration

tr.text: Pracinasala the son of Upamanyu, Satyayajna the son of Pulusa, Indradyumna the son of Bhallavi, Jana the son of Sarkaraksa, and Budila the son of Asvatarasva – these five great householders and great Vedic scholars, having come together, held a discussion on ‘What is our Atman ? What is Brahman ?’

sa: उद्दालको वै भगवन्तो ऽयम् आरुणिः संप्रतीमम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् अध्येति ।
iast: uddālako vai bhagavanto ’yam āruṇiḥ saṃpratīmam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram adhyeti ।
words: name of Uddālaka (a renowned Brāhmaṇa teacher)

tr.text: They reflected among themselves, ‘Revered sirs, Uddalaka, the son of Aruna, knows well this Vaisvanara Atman. Well, let us go to him’. And they went to him.

words: a Brāhman versed in the Veda
an exclamation or inceptive particle (expressive of an exhortation to do anythin

tr.text: Uddalaka reflected, ‘These great householders and great Vedic scholars are going to uestion me; but possibly I shall not be able to tell them everything. However, I shall direct them to another teacher’.

sa: अश्वपतिर् वै भगवन्तो ऽयं कैकेयः संप्रतीमम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् अध्येति ।
iast: aśvapatir vai bhagavanto ’yaṃ kaikeyaḥ saṃpratīmam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram adhyeti ।

tr.text: Uddalaka said to the, ‘Revered sirs, at present, Asvapati, the son of Kekaya, is studying this Vaisvanara Atman. Well, let us go to him’. Then they went to him.

sa: तेभ्यो ह प्राप्तेभ्यः पृथग् अर्हाणि कारयां चकार ।
न मे स्तेनो जनपदे न कदर्यो न मद्यपः ।
नानाहिताग्निर् नाविद्वान् न स्वैरी स्वैरिणी कुतः ।
यावद् एकैकस्मा ऋत्विजे धनं दास्यामि तावद् भगवद्भ्यो दास्यामि ।
iast: tebhyo ha prāptebhyaḥ pṛthag arhāṇi kārayāṃ cakāra ।
na me steno janapade na kadaryo na madyapaḥ ।
nānāhitāgnir nāvidvān na svairī svairiṇī kutaḥ ।
yāvad ekaikasmā ṛtvije dhanaṃ dāsyāmi tāvad bhagavadbhyo dāsyāmi ।
words: one who has not performed the Agnyādhāna
the prize of a contest or the contest itself (lit. a running match)

tr.text: When they arrived, the king arranged for each of them separately a welcome with suitable rites. Next morning, on rising, he said to them, ‘In my kingdom there is no thief, no miser, no drunkard, no man who has not installed the fire, no ignorant person, no adulterer, so how can there be any adulteress ? Revered sirs, I am going to perform a sacrifice. In that as much wealth, sirs, as I give to each single priest, shall I give to you also. Revered sirs, please remain’.

sa: येन हैवार्थेन पुरुषश् चरेत् तं हैव वदेत् ।
iast: yena haivārthena puruṣaś caret taṃ haiva vadet ।

tr.text: They said, ‘The purpose for which a man goes (to another), on that alone he should speak to him. You are, at present, studying the Vaisvanara Atman, please tell us of that.

words: the earlier part of the day

tr.text: The king said to them, ‘I shall answer you in the morning’. In the morning, they approached him with sacrificial fuel in their hands. The king, without receiving them as initiated pupils, spoke thus:

sa: औपमन्यव कं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्स इति ।
दिवम् एव भगवो राजन्न् इति होवाच ।
एष वै सुतेजा आत्मा वैश्वानरो यं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्से ।
तस्मात् तव सुतं प्रसुतम् आसुतं कुले दृश्यते ॥
iast: aupamanyava kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti ।
divam eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca ।
eṣa vai sutejā ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse ।
tasmāt tava sutaṃ prasutam āsutaṃ kule dṛśyate ॥
words: the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)

tr.text: ‘O Aupamanyava, what is the Atman on which you meditate ?’ He replied, ‘Heaven only, O venerable king’. The king said, ‘This that you meditate upon as Atman is the Vaisvanara Atman known as "the highly luminous". Therefore in your family are seen the Suta, Prasuta and Asuta libations of Soma-juice.’

sa: अत्त्य् अन्नं पश्यति प्रियम् भवत्य् अस्य ब्रह्मवर्चसं कुले ये एतम् एवम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् उपास्ते ।
मूधा त्व् एष आत्मन इति होवाच ।
मूर्धा ते व्यपतिष्यद् यन् मां नागमिष्य इति ॥
iast: atty annaṃ paśyati priyam bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ye etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste ।
mūdhā tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca ।
mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti ॥
words: to fly or dash or rush through

tr.text: ‘So you eat food and see what is dear. One who meditates on this Vaisvanara Atman thus, eats food and sees what is dear, and there is in his family the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom. But this is only the head of the Atman. If you had not come to me your head (a portion) would have fallen down.’

sa: प्राचीनयोग्य कं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्स इति ।
आदित्यम् एव भगवो राजन्न् इति होवाच ।
एष वै विश्वरूप आत्मा वैश्वानरो यं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्ते ।
तस्मात् तव बहु विश्वरूपं कुले दृश्यते ॥
iast: prācīnayogya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti ।
ādityam eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca ।
eṣa vai viśvarūpa ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāste ।
tasmāt tava bahu viśvarūpaṃ kule dṛśyate ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: Then the king said to Satyayajna Paulusi, ‘O Pracinayogya, what is that Atman on which you meditate ?’ He replied, ‘The sun only, O venerable king’. The king said, ‘This that you meditate upon as Atman is the Vaisvanara Atman known as "the multiform". Therefore in your family are seen all kinds of enjoyable things.

sa: अत्त्य् अन्नं पश्यति प्रियं भवत्य् अस्य ब्रह्मवर्चसं कुले य एतम् एवम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् उपास्ते ।
चक्षुष् ट्व् एतद् आत्मन इति होवाच ।
अन्धो ऽभविष्यो यन् मां नागमिष्य इति ॥
iast: atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste ।
cakṣuṣ ṭv etad ātmana iti hovāca ।
words: to roll or go onwards (as a carriage)
a golden ornament for the neck or breast

tr.text: ‘So, for you are provided a chariot drawn by mules, maid-servants and a gold necklace; so you eat food and see what is dear. One who thus meditates upon this Vaisvanara Atman, eats food and sees what is dear, and there is in his family the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom. But this is only the eye of the Atman. If you had not come to me you would have become blind.’

sa: वैयाघ्रपद्य कं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्स इति ।
वायुम् एव भगवो राजन्न् इति होवाच ।
एष वै पृथग्वर्त्मात्मा वैश्वानरो यं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्से ।
तस्मात् त्वां पृथग् बलय आयन्ति पृथग् रथश्रेणयो ऽनुयन्ति ॥
iast: vaiyāghrapadya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti ।
vāyum eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca ।
eṣa vai pṛthagvartmātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse ।
tasmāt tvāṃ pṛthag balaya āyanti pṛthag rathaśreṇayo ’nuyanti ॥
words: the track or rut of a wheel

tr.text: Then the king said to Indradyumna Bhallaveya, ‘O descendant of Vyaghrapada, what is that Atman on which you meditate ?’ He replied, ‘Air only, O venerable king.’ The king said, ‘This that you meditate upon as Atman is the Vaisvanara Atman known as "the diversely coursed". Therefore from diverse directions offerings come to you, and various rows of chariots follow you.

sa: अत्त्य् अन्नं पश्यति प्रियं भवत्य् अस्य ब्रह्मवर्चसं कुले य एतम् एवम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् उपास्ते ।
प्राणस् त्व् एष आत्मन इति होवाच ।
प्राणस् त उदक्रमिष्यद् यन् मां नागमिष्य इति ॥
iast: atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste ।
prāṇas tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca ।
prāṇas ta udakramiṣyad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti ॥

tr.text: ‘So you eat food and see what is dear. One who thus meditates upon this Vaisvanara Atman eats food and sees what is dear, and there is in his family the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom. But this is only the Prana of the Atman. If you had not come to me your Prana would have departed’.

tr.text: Therefore, even if one, who knows thus, offers the remnant of his food to a Chandala, then also that food becomes his offering to the Vaisvanara Atman only. There is this verse about it.
